newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo platinum futures rise on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo platinum futures rise on short-covering.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum futures ended higher as short-covering gathered momentum, supported by the fact December spot expiry ended smoothly, traders said.
The December spot contract expired at noon, up one yen per gram at 1,351 yen, with 885 lots of deliveries.
Active short-covering boosted spot platinum prices as platinum was quoted at $372.00/75 per ounce at the Tokyo close, after opening at $368.75/369.50.
"The platinum futures market was supported as one concern disappeared after the spot December contract expired steady," one trader said.
Traders had feared that the December platinum contract might fall sharply ahead of the expiry, pressured by massive long positions in the December contract.
Other platinum futures ranged from 16 yen to 19 yen per gram higher, with benchmark October ending up 17 yen at 1,358 yen.

Some traders said the firm spot expiry in the December platinum contract was partly attributable to traders' willingness to take deliveries due to the delay in Japan's year-end platinum talks with Russia.
Gold futures ended higher in tandem with platinum.

Spot December contract of gold futures expired at noon at 1,347 yen, with 3,413 lots of deliveries. Other gold prices ranged from three to eight yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark October ending up eight at 1,339 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $369.30/60 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $368.40/80 in New York on Tuesday.

Traders said sentiment in gold remained bearish as the topside of $370 could be tough to break through for the near-term. Benchmark silver October ended up 1.1 yen per 10 grams firmer at 179.5 yen, while benchmark palladium October contract was two yen per gram up at 430 yen.
